subject: Priv infra: CI dependency scan, module ownership & GitOps parity
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Julius Kramer <julius@edgeworks.com>, EdgeWorks SRE <sre+infra@edgeworks.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priv infra: CI dependency scan, module ownership & GitOps parity

Team / Julius —

Quick summary from the automated dependency & parity scan we ran against the EdgeWorks private-deploy repo (attached CSV + checklist): a handful of blockers surfaced that impact both security posture and our ability to hand off a GitOps flow to EdgeWorks SRE. I tried to separate quick wins from items needing design work.

High-level findings (see attached dependency-scan-20270520.csv + gitops-parity-checklist.md):
- Terraform: four modules reference cross-account IAM roles with broad actions (s3:*, iam:PassRole). Owner not well-defined; module tags are missing owner metadata.
- Helm: chart values rely on images hosted on public registries; EdgeWorks runs air-gapped mirror — imagePullSecrets missing from the chart values as templated inputs.
- Ansible: playbooks contain a fallback path that reads plaintext creds from a legacy vault file when Vault endpoint is unreachable. Needs hardening (Ansible Vault / KMS).
- CI: terragrunt/terraform versions mismatch between the repo's preflight job and the runner image; several runs fail with plan-time errors.
- Networking: the network diagram attached shows a control-plane subnet with permissive egress (0.0.0.0/0) in a couple staging modules — we should restrict to necessary control-plane IP ranges and add explicit NACLs where appropriate.

Recommended next steps (proposal):
1) We triage and classify each finding as "low-risk (code only)", "infra change (needs ops window)", or "policy change (legal/compliance)".
2) For low-risk fixes (helm value inputs, version pinning, small terraform lint updates) we target EOW May 28.
3) Infra / network changes (NACLs, rework of cross-account roles) will go behind a short RFC and aim for a 2-week timeline (impacting rollout windows) — propose a maintenance window with EdgeWorks.
4) Add a preflight GitHub Actions job to validate image mirror entries, terraform version, and a lightweight network policy sanity check before merge. I opened a draft PR stub for that (attached diff).

Questions for EdgeWorks:
- Can you confirm the image mirror hostnames and allowed egress CIDRs for control-plane VMs?
- Any explicit constraints on accepting role scope changes (e.g., legal restriction on iam:PassRole)?

Julius — tagging you to ask whether we should hold on any changes until your internal compliance review completes.

Attachments: dependency-scan-20270520.csv, edgeworks-network-diagram.png, gitops-parity-checklist.md

—
Chloe Martin
Staff SRE (Private Deploy)
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Julius Kramer <julius@edgeworks.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks SRE <sre+infra@edgeworks.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priv infra: CI dependency scan, module ownership & GitOps parity

Chloe — thanks for the quick run and clear breakdown. We reviewed the attachments internally and added a short constraints doc (attached). A few immediate notes from EdgeWorks SRE: 

- Airgap requirements: we must mirror all base images into our local Harbor instance; we can provide the mirror hostnames but not the public pull endpoints. Helm changes are fine but we need templated values for image registry/namespace and imagePullSecrets out of the box.
- IAM: we cannot accept iam:PassRole changes that allow cross-tenant role assumption. We can accept scoped service roles limited to s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject for our artifact buckets, and narrow KMS decrypt for signed artifacts.
- Networking: control-plane egress must be restricted to our oob-management CIDR (10.248.16.0/24) and specific vendor update endpoints — we can't open 0.0.0.0/0 from the control-plane.
- CI runners: our on-prem runners run Ubuntu 20.04 with self-hosted GitHub Actions; they include only Terraform 1.2.9. We can run a custom container for builds if needed but prefer avoiding ad-hoc runner scripts.

We attached: edgeworks-ci-constraints.pdf (short policy), and a clean copy of our mirror registry hostnames.

We agree with the proposed triage approach. For anything classified as "infra change", we need an explicit RFC and wargame notes. If your team can provide the RFC draft by next Tue (May 25), we can schedule a joint maintenance window for the subsequent two-week sprint.

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Julius Kramer <julius@edgeworks.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra: CI dependency scan, module ownership & GitOps parity

Thanks — I ran a quick internal triage with Aditya and Grace this morning and here's a proposed breakdown & owners for the fixes. I've included rough ETA buckets.

Low-risk (code changes, no infra window) — target: EOW 2027-05-28
- Helm: add variables for image.registry, image.namespace, image.pullSecretName; update README with mirror instructions. Owner: Grace O'Connor.
- CI: pin terraform/terragrunt in the preflight job; add version check step. Owner: Aditya Rao.
- Linting: run tflint + helm lint in the same preflight. Owner: Aditya Rao.

Medium-risk (config + small infra, needs coordination) — target: 2 weeks
- Ansible: remove plaintext fallback and integrate Ansible Vault with KMS-backed secrets. Owner: Irene Choi.
- Module metadata: add module_owner tag and a module-owners.yaml at repo root; add CODEOWNERS entries for TF modules. Owner: Chloe Martin.

High-risk (requiring RFC / maintenance window) — target: 2-3 weeks after RFC sign-off
- Cross-account roles: refactor to use explicit short-lived service token exchange with minimal scopes. We will propose replacing broad iam:PassRole usage with a scoped federation pattern. Owner: Aditya Rao + EdgeWorks SRE.
- Networking: restrict control-plane egress by introducing NACLs and a managed NAT gateway with explicit allow list. Owner: Network Ops + EdgeWorks SRE.

Immediate actions I've already taken today:
- Opened a draft GH PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/412) with the preflight job skeleton and basic lint steps. The PR includes the pinning diff (attached as preflight-github-actions-pr.diff).
- Added an issue template for RFCs under /docs/rfcs/priv-deploy.

Requests from our side to EdgeWorks for the RFC:
- Provide the egress CIDR list and mirror hostnames by EOB Mon May 24 so we can code the preflight checks and helm defaults.

If EdgeWorks confirms constraints, we'll merge low-risk changes and then start the RFC process for cross-account roles & network changes. I'll set up a 30-minute sync on Tue (May 25) to walk through the RFC outline.

—
Irene Choi
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra: CI dependency scan, module ownership & GitOps parity

Thanks, everyone — plan sounds good and pragmatic. Julius, appreciate the constraints doc; we'll treat iam:PassRole as a blocker and not propose changes that expand privileges beyond what you allowed.

Action items (confirmed):
- Grace: helm chart changes + README for mirror usage (deliverable: PR by 2027-05-26).
- Aditya: preflight CI job PR (PR #412) — finish pinning + lint steps (deliverable: PR update by 2027-05-24).
- Irene: migrate Ansible secrets to Vault + KMS (deliverable: initial branch by 2027-06-02).
- Chloe/Aditya: draft RFC for cross-account role refactor (deliverable: RFC draft by 2027-05-25).
- EdgeWorks: provide mirror hostnames and egress CIDR list by EOB Mon 2027-05-24.

I'll circulate a short meeting invite for Tue May 25 10:00 PT to walk the RFC outline and confirm the maintenance window cadence. If EdgeWorks is comfortable with the schedule, we will merge the low-risk PRs as soon as they're green and then move to RFC sign-off for infra changes.

Attachments: dependency-scan-20270520.csv, edgeworks-network-diagram.png, preflight-github-actions-pr.diff

Please reply with any blocking concerns; otherwise I'll take these as accepted and kick off the RFC work.

—
